crossrefs.text: But I also have a mind; I am not inferior to you. Who does not know such things as these?
Though the arrogant have smeared me with lies, I keep Your precepts with all my heart.
Even a fool is considered wise if he keeps silent, and discerning when he holds his tongue.
“Present your case,” says the LORD. “Submit your arguments,” says the King of Jacob.
Then the LordGod formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.
Then Abraham answered, “Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord—though I am but dust and ashes—
and terror and dread will fall on them. By the power of Your arm they will be as still as a stone until Your people pass by, O LORD, until the people You have bought pass by.
Then the LORD said to Moses, “Write this on a scroll as a reminder and recite it to Joshua, because I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven.”
Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.
Yet He knows the way I have taken; when He has tested me, I will come forth as gold.
But I know that my Redeemer lives, and in the end He will stand upon the earth.
If you say, ‘Let us persecute him, since the root of the matter lies with him,’
For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers,
neither height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Even if our hearts condemn us, God is greater than our hearts, and He knows all things.
I will never say that you are right; I will maintain my integrity until I die.
His anger burns against me, and He counts me among His enemies.
He puts my feet in the stocks; He watches over all my paths.’
Remember not the sins of my youth, nor my rebellious acts; remember me according to Your loving devotion, because of Your goodness, O LORD.
How long, O LORD? Will You forget me forever? How long will You hide Your face from me?
The Lord is like an enemy; He has swallowed up Israel. He has swallowed up all her palaces and destroyed her strongholds. He has multiplied mourning and lamentation for the Daughter of Judah.

Then the man and his wife heard the voice of the LordGod walking in the garden in the breeze of the day, and they hid themselves from the presence of the LordGod among the trees of the garden. But the LordGod called out to the man, “Where are you?” “I heard Your voice in the garden,” he replied, “and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid myself.”
Please do not let her be like a stillborn infant whose flesh is half consumed when he comes out of his motherʼs womb.”
He said: “I will hide My face from them; I will see what will be their end. For they are a perverse generation— children of unfaithfulness.
